surfaces.part: top band / roof slab of the confessional
gold valances over the curtain bays

answer.evidence: Rows 8-14 form a wide orange band, 46 px across. Its top row is the outline at row 8, and rows 9-11 are mid-tone. Row 12 is a lighter line (#d59147) that acts as the front-edge line. Rows 13-14 are darker (#744e2c, then #2a180b) and act as eave shadow, with a small gold ornament hanging below. This matches the 'cabinet: top 5 + edge + eave' reference. Below it the front face runs from row 15 to row 47 and holds the purple curtains, the central door with its lattice window, and a base plinth at rows 43-47. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The outlines are tinted dark brown beside the wood and dark purple beside the curtains. Neutral edge share is 0%, so this matches Beodeul's approach rather than a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is only 3%, and the lattice window, gold cornice trim and curtain folds add some texture. The weakness is depth. It has 18 distinct colours against 38-40 for the two comparable large props (the stall and the roofed well). Its per-tile median of 10 is also well below their 17-20, and only level with the small hedge. The wood body and curtains read as about 4 steps each, not the 5-6 on the stall and well. The large dark brown side panels and the door look fairly plain beside the per-plank grain and per-tile highlights on the references. It is clean and consistent, but a careful artist would likely see it as slightly thinner than the stall and well. With the instruction to fail when in doubt, this is a fail.

surfaces.part: top cornice band of the main body

answer.evidence: Rows 9-11 form a lighter orange band across the full width. Row 12 is a lighter edge line (#d59147), and rows 13-14 are dark eave shadow. Below that is a front face of about 33 rows (15-47) with purple curtained side bays, a central grated window and a door. The base plinth is at rows 42-47. The dark vertical strip on the left is a post on the front face, not a receding side face. The top band is thin at about 4 rows including the edge line, but it has a distinct edge line and shadow, so it counts as a top surface rather than a plain rim.

styleAnswer.evidence: The outline is tinted dark brown, with 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so it matches the Beodeul approach. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is only 3%, so there are no big flat areas. The weak point is richness. The candidate has 18 distinct colours and a median of 10 per tile. The comparable-size props, the cheese stall and the roofed well, have 38-40 colours and a median of 17-20 per tile. In the picture, the wood frame, cornice and door panel look like about 3-4 value steps, and the purple curtains look like 2-3 steps. There is little per-plank grain or per-element highlighting, and the large wood facade reads as simpler and flatter than the stall and well, which carry 5-6 steps and dense texture. It is cleanly built but noticeably less rich than the same-scale references.

surfaces.part: front face (booth with purple curtains, central door, base)

answer.evidence: Rows 9-11 are a lighter orange plank band. Row 12 is a brighter front-edge line (#d59147), followed by dark shadow rows 13-14 (L≈28-85). This matches the green cabinet reference of a top band, edge line and eave shadow. Below it the front face runs from row 15 to 47 with curtained stalls, a lattice window and a door. The band is about 4 rows, so it is a modest top surface rather than a 1-2 row rim. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's dark edges are tinted brown and none are neutral (0% near-neutral), so the outline is dark_material_tone rather than a sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is only 3%, and the median of 10 colours per tile matches the hedge reference. The weak point is the whole piece. It is about as large as the stall and the well, which have 40 and 38 distinct colours, but it has only 18. The wood frame and cornice show about 4 lightness steps, and the purple curtains look like 2-3 steps. The door lattice and wood panels read as fairly smooth, with little grain or per-plank highlighting compared with the stall and well. It is clean and tidy, but next to those references it looks thinner and flatter in ramp depth and texture. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: front face: curtained booths and central door

answer.evidence: The top band at rows 8-14 is 46px wide against the 44px body, so it overhangs. Rows 9-11 are a lighter wood surface (L~121-127). Row 12 is a distinctly lighter front-edge line (#d59147, L~157). Rows 13-14 are darker eave shadow (L 85 and 28). That makes a top surface of about 4 rows (9-12) with an edge line and shadow, as in the green cabinet reference. Below it the front face runs from row 15 to about row 43: curtained booths, a central door with a lattice window, and a base plinth at rows 44-47. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, and by eye the outline is dark brown beside the wood, so it reads as dark_material_tone rather than a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is only 3%, which is lower than the stall's 13%. The median of 10 colours per 16x16 tile equals the hedge and is a little below the stall (17) and well (20). Its 18 total colours are above the bench and hedge (14 and 11) but well below the stall and well (about 40), which are bigger multi-material pieces. The wood frame, cornice and door lattice show about 4-5 wood steps with grain bands. The purple curtains and gold sign are shallower, at about 2-3 steps each. It is slightly less rich than the best references but is structured and textured, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.
